item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It provides the exact required API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption behavior, validates inputs, and creates a replayable multipart body. B deliberately expands and changes the API and retry machinery beyond scope.","reasons":["A has the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption).","A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), satisfying the required multipart field, filename, buffering, and helper reuse.","A retains Add unchanged apart from documentation and applies the existing FilesOption configuration to Upload.","A's retry test verifies multipart content on both attempts after a 429, while B also tests retry but through an unnecessarily expanded implementation scope and API surface."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request construction, option application, response decoding, and missing-data handling instead of routing the encoded body through Add as explicitly required.","The visible tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or source-reader failures, despite those cases being required."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public signature, accepting ...UploadFileOption instead of ...FilesOption.","It adds association fields and multiple WithUpload* APIs, directly contradicting the contract.","It introduces NewForm instead of using NewFile directly and expands the internal multipart helper without need (though NewFile delegates to it). It also bypasses FilesService.Add entirely and fails to preserve existing FilesOption behavior for Upload callers by creating a separate option system. It refactors RawClient retry behavior for all io.ReadSeeker bodies, an explicitly forbidden unrelated retry-machinery change with subtle shared-seeker and concurrent-replay risks. The visible tests omit source-reader error coverage."]}
